questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Please explain: *
Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Country with a dialect I would be interested in.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: To be honest I think it was complicated regarding Visa after 14 days and after 3 months. Those things are difficult if you're not fluent in the language. School information regarding first day, and other important dates was okay. On the other hand we have the WhatsApp numbers of the people who work with international students. They made a WhatsApp group and explained for example the visa process, this was good.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Yes, somewhat.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I personally think it's overwhelming, but everyone seemed to have an okay time. I had a roomie, and we found our apartment on Facebook before arrival. But it was somewhat far from campus but not more than 15minutes by taxi. I think it was possible to find cheaper, and closer.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Public transportation isn't that great, they have the BRT bus which is okay, and coaster (never rode a coaster/mini bus because they were overwhelming). It is possible though, but taxi/uber/jeeny/careem is easier.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I think it was done beforehand in my case.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer:
I think it was automatic in our case...
If you mean in regards to levels, I think the test was a bit off, but it is possible to try other levels and see if it works out.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: It is possible to write to the people for th international affairs department through WhatsApp.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Yes

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I was on level 4 which was perfect for me. The level contained 2 days reading, 1 day grammar and writing, 1 day listening/dialect and 1 day talking, and class was 4 hours a day. The teachers speak mainly arabic. To be honest I would recommend a class where you feel that you match the level of the other students also, rather than only focusing on the material. Since the material is really good regardless of level.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: More classical, I liked it. The way they teach grammar is different.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Arabic for non-arabic speakers level 4.

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your second semester. *
What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Arabic for non-arabic speakers level 4.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Taxi, since bus wasn't very suitable for me. Living 15 minutes away from camps by taxi would be about 20+/- dkk each way.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
Some food can be less expensive but some things are the same prices as Denmark.
Taxi is definitely less expensive than Denmark.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There was an art club.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Jorda university is pretty big, the have some sports clubs and art club.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The art club was nice enough, though I only went 5 times.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Language center has trip different cities almost every Saturday which is really nice.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Yes, though speaking dialect is difficult.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Language exchange, lots of students are interested in English.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None in particular.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: People are very outgoing and curious to know about foreigners. And excited to have a conversation.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
(1) A lot of students find their apartment in Jordan, and not beforehand.

(2) If you choose an apartment a bit far, research how the commute would be beforehand, especially if you wish to use public transportation.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: You might find a better apartment physically searching for it in Jordan, instead of doing it before coming. I didn't though, because I found the thought of it too overwhelming, I think our apartment was okay, 2 bedrooms and 1 livingroom which costed us around 420JD in total, and it was around 15minutes by car to reach the language center. But a lot of people said that might be not the best price.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: At te end of the semester we understand most of simple arabic speech by our teachers in class. In the beginning the ears needed to get used to it.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Speaking dialect in real life with strangers.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
